title: pvVisItBOVReader
body:
## pvVisItBOVReader

Reads VisIt's BOV (brick of values) format: a short text header (.bov) giving DATA_FILE, DATA_SIZE, DATA_FORMAT, BRICK_ORIGIN, BRICK_SIZE, VARIABLE and CENTERING for one raw binary array on a regular grid. The output is a rectilinear-grid block named "mesh" carrying that one variable. Use pvImageReader instead for raw volumes without a BOV header, where you supply dimensions, spacing and data type yourself. FileName takes a list of files, each one time step of a series (ParaView's file-series wrapper).

Common mistakes and assumptions:

- Whether the variable appears in PointArrayStatus or CellArrayStatus depends on the header's CENTERING (NODAL or ZONAL); select it in the matching list.
- Multi-component data arrive as one vector array; VisIt's real/imaginary expressions are not converted by the bridge.
- Name the arrays you need in PointArrayStatus and CellArrayStatus: the VisIt bridge starts with every variable unselected, so omitting them normally gives geometry without fields.
- Schemaxis generates this binding from ParaView's catalogue and has not run a native acceptance check for this reader; check meshes, arrays and times on your own data.

Native constructor: `VisItBOVReader`. Identity: `sources/VisItBOVReader`. Role: `pipeline`. Output kinds: `["data"]`.

### Inputs

No connected inputs (source/resource).


### Options

| Key | Meaning / native assignment | Type and constraints | Default / required | Example value |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `CellArrayStatus` | Names of the zone-centred (cell) variables to read from BOV data; each becomes a cell-data array on every selected mesh that defines it. Vector variables arrive as one multi-component array, while VisIt expressions and tensor, label, species and array variables are not converted by the bridge. The BOV plugin offers the one variable named by VARIABLE in the header; CENTERING NODAL makes it a point array and ZONAL a cell array; which of them appear here depends on how each is centred in the file. | `{"items":{"type":"string"},"type":"array"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `["REPLACE_WITH_VALUE"]` |
| `FileName` | The list of files to be read by the reader. Fixed at construction; cannot vary per visit. | `{"items":{"minLength":1,"type":"string"},"minItems":1,"type":"array"}` | `required` | `["REPLACE_WITH_VALUE"]` |
| `MaterialStatus` | Names of materials to convert into volume-fraction cell arrays. For each selected material the bridge adds a float cell array named after it: 1 in cells made only of that material, its volume fraction in mixed cells and -1 where it is absent. The BOV plugin defines no materials, so this list has nothing to select. | `{"items":{"type":"string"},"type":"array"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `["REPLACE_WITH_VALUE"]` |
| `MeshStatus` | Names of the BOV meshes to read. Each selected mesh becomes one named block of the multiblock output and unlisted meshes are skipped. The BOV plugin reports one rectilinear mesh named "mesh"; with DIVIDE_BRICK its bricklets become separate domains of that block. | `{"items":{"type":"string"},"type":"array"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `["REPLACE_WITH_VALUE"]` |
| `PointArrayStatus` | Names of the node-centred (point) variables to read from BOV data; each becomes a point-data array on every selected mesh that defines it. Vector variables arrive as one multi-component array, while VisIt expressions and tensor, label, species and array variables are not converted by the bridge. The BOV plugin offers the one variable named by VARIABLE in the header; CENTERING NODAL makes it a point array and ZONAL a cell array; which of them appear here depends on how each is centred in the file. | `{"items":{"type":"string"},"type":"array"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `["REPLACE_WITH_VALUE"]` |

Execution contract:

```json
{
  "mode": "serial",
  "performance": "unknown"
}
```

Coverage and unbound native properties:

```json
{
  "defaults": "native defaults for omitted options",
  "gaps": {},
  "origin": "generated",
  "output": "native inspection required; explicit output-port selection available",
  "outputPorts": null,
  "qualification": "not-run"
}
```

### Syntax example

Place in `nodes`. Data outputs may be selected by a scene; resource outputs must be connected to a compatible consumer.

```json
{
  "id": "result",
  "filter": "pvVisItBOVReader",
  "options": {
    "FileName": [
      "REPLACE_WITH_VALUE"
    ]
  }
}
```
